questions: How many devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed coherent parity oscillations?
Why were the others set aside?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown, for example other in-plane fields than B|| = 150 mT, higher temperatures, coupler amplitudes above 11.25 mV, and longer pulse durations?
What does the second-best device or dataset look like? Fig. ED9 is a second tuning of the same device; is there a second device with even and odd manifolds compared?

Methods III says "A successful tuning is indicated by oscillations with similar frequencies and contrast in both manifolds." How many tunings did you try, and how many were set aside because the even and odd frequencies or contrasts differed?

Since the frequency difference in Fig. 3b bounds only the product of the two chains' overlaps, can you bound each chain separately, for example from the time-domain data near phi = pi (Fig. 2e) or by detuning one outer dot at a time?
For the charge-qubit comparison in Fig. 4g,h, did you sweep the coupler amplitude in the double-dot configuration, and would oscillations decaying within a few ns be resolved with your pulse timing?
Fig. 3h-j are described as "Separate representative measurements", and a charge jump preceded Fig. 2e: how were these traces chosen, and were any datasets set aside because of the jump or drift?
